"Spin-off" from discussion in #775 - conclusion by @jmanico:

[5.5.3](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x13-V5-Validation-Sanitization-Encoding.md#v55-deserialization-prevention-requirements)

Current V5.3.3 is duplicate of V14.2.1 and not actionable

> V5.5.3 Verify that deserialization of untrusted data is avoided or is protected in both custom code and third-party libraries (such as JSON, XML and YAML parsers).

> V14.2.1 Verify that all components are up to date, preferably using a dependency checker during build or compile time.

Milestone v4.1

comments.body:
5.3.3 to me is similar to saying "please stop SQL injection" without 
explaining how to do it.

To stop deserialization attacks requires a multi-pronged strategy. Here 
is a more nuanced strategy we should somehow capture in 4.1

1) Keep your JSON and XML parsers up to date, this involves keeping both 
framework and 3rd party library code updated via 14.2.1

2) One must filter incoming binary data to limit what classes may be 
deserialized - this is different for every language but in Java it's JEP 
290 https://openjdk.java.net/jeps/290

3) One must also design objects with deserialization in mind which is 
really detailed - 
https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/seccodeguide.html#8 is a 
good Java specific example of object design for deserialization

4) Deserialization of binary data done right by requirements covered in 
the Oracle secure coding guidelines are complex an you are better off 
avoiding it or using XML/JSON instead

- Jim
